title: Babur Problems Of The Eastern Areas And The Afghans
definition: The consolidation of Mughal power in the Gangetic plains (Bihar and Bengal) following the Battle of Panipat (1526), characterized by the persistent resistance of Afghan chieftains who viewed the Mughals as foreign usurpers.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the transition from Lodi to Mughal rule and the geopolitical instability in Eastern India that necessitated the Battle of Ghaghara.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Babur Problems Of The Eastern Areas And The Afghans.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Political map of North India post-1526
